title: api: schema versioning - deprecations, beta headers, backward-compat shims for streaming and OpenAI-compat
author: Priya Nair
description:
Context: As part of our push to stabilize streaming, structured outputs, and the OpenAI compatibility layer we need a predictable API versioning story. Clients have started adopting new structured output fields and function/tool-calling semantics; to avoid breaking production clients we add explicit version negotiation, deprecation headers, and a set of backward-compatibility shims that map new responses into legacy shapes.

What this PR does (single continuous description): Adds an API version negotiation header (X-Redwood-API-Version) and an opt-in beta header (X-Redwood-Beta: schema_v2) which enables the new structured response schema including: structured.output (object with choices[] -> message.content structured variants), first-class tool_call objects and deterministic function calling hints. For clients that do not opt in, we introduce a compatibility shim layer that on-the-fly transforms the v2 structured response into a legacy v1-compatible shape (text + choices[].text) and emits deprecation warnings via the X-Redwood-Deprecation header and a per-response X-Redwood-Deprecation-Warning with guidance and migration link.

Streaming notes: Streaming semantics are preserved. We add a small compatibility mode in runtime/streaming to emit both SSE "data: {legacy_chunk}" events and the new "data: {structured_chunk}" events when both X-Redwood-Beta and OpenAI-Compat headers are present. This prevents breaking existing SSE/OpenAI-compatible consumers while allowing new clients to process structured deltas. Edgecases handled: KV-cache partials, mid-message function_call boundaries, and newline-only chunks are normalized so event boundaries remain consistent across adapters.

OpenAI-compat adapter: The OpenAI compatibility layer (src/api/compat/openai_adapter.py) gains a version-aware adapter that will: 1) accept OpenAI-style requests and attach compatibility headers if requested, 2) translate new tool_call/structured outputs into the OpenAI completion/chat shapes when the OpenAI-Compat header is present, 3) preserve streaming SSE framing for OpenAI-style clients. This reduces the migration friction for downstream internal customers using OpenAI-compatible SDKs.

Deprecation policy and rollout: Deprecation warnings are returned in responses for legacy fields (choices[].text, top_level.text) with a migration URL to docs/migration/api-schema-versioning.md. We plan a 90-day deprecation window: warnings start immediately for non-opt-in clients, a soft-fail gated enforcement period at 60 days will surface errors in the admin console, and strict enforcement will begin after 90 days for new clients only. Existing clients will still receive VM-level compatibility shims for 12 months to avoid accidental outages.

Tests and observability: Adds integration tests for header negotiation, streaming boundary conditions, and OpenAI-compat translation. Adds metrics: api.version_negotiation.count, api.deprecation_warnings.count, api.compat_shim_latency.p50/p95. Dashboard and a new alert (APIVersionMismatchRate) were added in observability-pack.

Docs: Migration guide and API reference updates under redwood-docs were added and linked from the deprecation header. The PR updates quickstarts and SDK notes with example header usage.

Rollout plan: Canary rollout to dedicated capacity first (1%), then hosted API (10%, 50%, 100%) over two weeks. Feature flag feature.api.schema_v2 controls the server-side toggle.

Checklist:
- [x] Version negotiation header implementation
- [x] Backcompat shims for v1 mapping
- [x] Streaming normalization and dual-emission compatibility mode
- [x] OpenAI-compat adapter updates
- [x] Integration tests and metrics
- [x] Docs and migration guide
- [x] Release notes entry

review_comments: Evan Brooks: Do we have a plan for non-SSE streaming transports (websockets) and how they will consume deprecation warnings?

Priya Nair (reply): Websocket clients will receive deprecation warnings in a control frame and the Compatibility shim will include legacy_text in the first data frame. Added tests for websocket framing.
Jordan Li: Need to ensure latency added by the shim is negligible; can we add the shim behind a fast path?

Priya Nair (reply): Shim is implemented as a zero-copy view where possible; added api.compat_shim_latency metrics and a p95 target of <1ms on 3090-equivalent. Note added to PR description and observability dashboard.
Megan O'Neil: Docs look good. Please add example curl commands with the beta header for both streaming and non-streaming flows.
Priya Nair (reply): Added curl examples to docs and examples/headers/README.md
ci_summary: Initial CI run: lint passed, unit tests passed, integration tests failed on streaming boundary (flaky newline handling). Fixed in commit 4. Rerun CI: all checks passed. Final status: pass
release_notes: Introduces API schema version negotiation (X-Redwood-API-Version) and an opt-in beta header (X-Redwood-Beta: schema_v2). Adds backward-compatibility shims to preserve legacy OpenAI-compatible and text-based clients. Deprecation warnings are emitted for legacy fields. See docs/migration/api-schema-versioning.md for migration steps.
